items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: Snoozer says he got his style from Peck Kelly. ... So, and he played with Whiteman behind the rhythm boys, and you couldn't hear him at all, and he played with our fair governor, Jimmy Davis, and you couldn't hear him at all behind him.

there's a very, very interesting story behind Snoozer Quinn's rendition, and that was Snoozer's Wanderings. And I want Mr. Johnny Wiggs to tell us just how that record was recorded. Well, I hope we have time to start at the beginning. I met Snoozer when Peck Kelly sent for me. Peck Kelly was considered one of the greatest piano players that ever lived. And he was playing in Freeport, and they sent for me, and I pulled out my horn to play the dinner session. And it was a big band in those days. That was supposed…

slam the door in nurses' faces. It was done out at the hospital, the TB hospital out the lake. I had to slam the door in audits' faces.
